references.text: The Levites were appointed to serve at the tabernacle of the testimony and bear responsibility for it, so that wrath would not come upon the congregation of Israel.
The Levites were to perform the service for Aaron and all the congregation before the tabernacle and take care of all the equipment in the tent of meeting.
The Levites were given to Aaron and his sons to serve in the tent of meeting and bear the guilt of the people of Israel, so that no disaster would strike them.
Aaron and his sons were to bear the guilt for offenses committed in the sanctuary, and the Levites were to assist them with the service.
The tithe that the Israelites give to the Lord is given to the Levites as an inheritance; therefore they shall have no inheritance among the people of Israel.
The tribe of Levi received no share of land with their brothers; the Lord is their inheritance, just as the Lord had promised them.
The Levitical priests and the whole tribe of Levi were to have no portion or inheritance with Israel; they were to live from the Lord's fire offerings and his inheritance.
Only the tribe of Levi was given no inheritance by Moses; the fire offerings of the Lord, the God of Israel, are their inheritance, as he had promised them.
The Levites received no share of the land like the other tribes, but they were given cities to live in with surrounding pasturelands.
Ezekiel confirms that the priests shall have no inheritance in Israel; the Lord himself is their inheritance.
